rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch deletes the entire locally-duplicated `im_convert_window_to_frame_coords` helper (along with `im_get_vfinger_position`, `im_is_point_outside_content`, and `inverse_point`) from input_manager.c. Every pointer-processing path is rewired to the display side: `sc_input_manager_get_position` calls `sc_screen_convert_window_to_frame_coords`, `sc_input_manager_process_touch` calls `sc_screen_convert_window_to_frame_coords`, `sc_input_manager_process_mouse_motion` calls `sc_screen_get_vfinger_position`, and `sc_input_manager_process_mouse_button` calls `sc_screen_is_point_outside_content` and `sc_screen_get_vfinger_position`. The corresponding implementations are added to screen.c (the display owner) with declarations in screen.h, restoring the single-owner geometry interpretation.
rubrics.criterion: The window-to-frame coordinate interpretation (content-rectangle normalization plus all client orientation variants) that the input component currently computes locally is no longer implemented on the input side: the locally duplicated conversion helper is removed and every pointer-processing path (shortcut position query, mouse motion, touch) obtains the mapping from the display side (a restored or equivalently re-homed single owner implementation).

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch deletes `im_is_point_outside_content` from input_manager.c and, in the mouse-button double-click path, replaces `im_is_point_outside_content(im->screen, event->x, event->y)` with `sc_screen_is_point_outside_content(im->screen, event->x, event->y)`. It defines `sc_screen_is_point_outside_content` in screen.c and declares it in screen.h, so the border-click containment decision is now reached through the display side rather than a local direct reader of `screen->rect` fields in the input component.
rubrics.criterion: The geometry decision predicate used by the mouse-button double-click path (whether the click point lies outside the displayed content rectangle) is no longer defined in the input component as a direct reader of the display rectangle fields; the containment decision is reached through the display side.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the input-local helpers im_get_vfinger_position, im_convert_window_to_frame_coords, and inverse_point from input_manager.c and adds a display-side sc_screen_get_vfinger_position in screen.c/screen.h. In sc_input_manager_process_mouse_button, the Ctrl/Shift virtual-finger path now calls sc_screen_get_vfinger_position(im->screen, event->x, event->y, im->vfinger_invert_x, im->vfinger_invert_y), and mouse_motion uses the same API. rubrics.evidence: The problem statement identifies the smell that the mouse-capture component "has been handed the whole display object, and it now inspects display-internal state to decide by itself when it is allowed to consume events." The agent.patch contains no changes to mouse_capture.c or mouse_capture.h, so the smell's capture-side relative-mode gate remains: sc_mouse_capture_is_relative_mode() still reads mc->screen->im.mp->relative_mode, sc_mouse_capture_handle_event() still returns false when that gate is false, and sc_screen_handle_event() still delegates without the display-side sc_screen_is_relative_mode() check. The patch only moves input_manager helpers to screen.c; it does not remove the capture subsystem's inspection of display state, so R4 is not satisfied.
rubrics.criterion: The mouse-capture component no longer inspects display state to decide whether it may consume events: the relative-mode gate that reads through the display object (window handle and the embedded input pipeline's mode flag) is not implemented inside the capture subsystem, and event delegation across the display event loop and the capture handler produces the same accept/forward outcomes as before.
